A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Flash-VAED work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and generation experiments, pruning and distillation ablations, and supplementary latency and scalability measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds temporal-consistency measurements, DAVIS reconstruction results, resource analyses and additional generalization experiments.

M1.justification: Independence-aware pruning, stage-specific operator replacement, shortcut injection and three-phase distillation remain unchanged, including the losses and backbone-specific pruning configurations. Appendix B applies existing optimizations to additional backbones and discusses potential extensions without introducing a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds reconstruction evaluation on the DAVIS 2019 Challenge test set at 720p, extending coverage to complex motion, occlusions and fine details. Training data, UCF-101 and VBench coverage are retained. Higher-resolution latency testing already existed in v1.

E2.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 11 add L1-norm channel pruning alongside the existing random-pruning comparator. New Table 7 also compares channel-pruning-only and operator-optimization-only variants. The principal LightVAE and Turbo-VAED comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds RAFT-based warping error, parameter-count and peak-VRAM measurements, and protocols for DAVIS evaluation and Causal Forcing deployment with seven selected VBench dimensions. Additional backbone diagnostics are also reported. The existing training settings and original benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The revision substantially expands diagnostic evidence: stronger pruning comparisons, component-specific resource ablations, DAVIS robustness testing, transfer to Causal Forcing, and SVD/operator-optimization analyses on HunyuanVideo and CogVideoX. The original resolution/frame-count study and training ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates for the experiments. The added SVD explained-variance results concern feature redundancy, not statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original table values are retained, while substantial new results appear. Table 2 reports Wan warping errors of 0.018662 for Flash-VAED and 0.026640 for LightVAE. DAVIS Table 6 reports corresponding PSNR values of 32.03 and 27.92. Table 7 adds memory and parameter results; Table 8 adds Causal Forcing scores, including multi-view consistency of 0.318 versus the original decoder's 0.424. New pruning curves, qualitative examples and additional-backbone findings further expand the evidence.

T1.justification: The method equations and Appendix A.1 computational-cost derivation are unchanged apart from numbering and formatting. New Equations 7–8 explain the adopted optical-flow warping metric; they do not introduce new theoretical reasoning, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same method, latent-alignment and efficiency claims, including approximately 6× decoding speedup, up to 96.9% reconstruction-performance retention and up to 36% pipeline acceleration. Added experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: New appendix discussions explain spatial generalization through convolutional structure, interpret component-specific resource savings, and discuss applicability to additional convolutional and transformer architectures. Appendix B.9 newly identifies failures involving tiny moving objects and dense faces, linking blur, flicker and detail loss to limited decoder capacity.

D1.justification: v2 documents implementation choices for added evaluations, including pretrained RAFT flow estimation from ground-truth frames and L1-based channel scoring from weights. Existing hardware, optimizer settings, loss coefficients, gradient masking, full prompts and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting DAVIS, temporal consistency, Causal Forcing and architectural/future-work discussion, while removing the Jetson technical brief and stereo-compression reference. The main related-work positioning remains stable. Publication updates and the retitled VLMQ reference concern retained works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are preserved. Changes include local wording and typo corrections, affiliation and acknowledgment updates, and expanded appendix organization. The original Appendix B.1–B.3 material is retained as B.6–B.8.

P2.justification: The document switches from a lab-branded format to an ICML layout, redesigning the opening page and rearranging or resizing existing displays. v2 adds four tables and two qualitative comparison figures, and redraws Figure 11 with an additional curve and revised axis ticks.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps: temporal measurements directly examine coherence after operator replacement, DAVIS tests challenging reconstruction conditions, and L1 pruning provides a stronger comparator than random pruning alone. Resource ablations and specific failure conditions also make the efficiency-quality tradeoff more assessable. Causal Forcing coverage remains selective and reveals a multi-view consistency gap, but the revision substantially strengthens the evidence and qualification of the central claims.
